items.note: S3's motivation says the network exchanges banks while restoring auxiliary values and S3.3 names three-element subsets, but there is no schedule, no copy/gather/scatter/side-injection maps, no cancellation of scratch values and no (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a).

S3.1 says that with frames at every vertex the intermediate frames cancel and each route applies only an endpoint operator, which is the content of the identity. It does not give the operator D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}, the edge change D_v D_u^{-1}, the sign, or the reason (a common frame commutes with a pointwise gate).
Only 'nested subspaces' is named. The plan has no triple indicator vectors or orthogonality, no terminal labels, no L=Ich, no Wm-2N+2L budget and no L<N/2.

S3.2 correctly gives the bit procedure's endpoint operator as the shear (H,D)->(H+D,D). It omits the matrix condition M_sink(rho(w)) - M_source(w) = I_m, the projection assignment with the negative source projection, and the rank sum s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b. It also wrongly says the endpoint shear is cheap by triangular factorization (see errors).

The plan says only that each procedure, the numerical one included, comes from its own fixed network. It has no phase frames C_U, no translation kernels aI+bX_v per residual vector, no s_c, and does not say the endpoint is C^{tensor m} or H_0 after diagonal corrections.

The plan states the key inequality s<Wm and that s/W<m gives the power saving. It does not separate the two networks' s_b and s_c, does not trace the saving to L<N/2, and gives no deficits eta or explicit tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}.
Controlled shifts and tape streams appear only as relies-on page names. No operation or O(V) bound is stated.

'Lower-triangular factorization' is named in S3.2, but A=E_1 Pi E_2 and the cost of exactly rank-many interchanges are absent. The name is also attached to the wrong operator: the endpoint shear instead of the edge shears.

S3.4 gives the recursion in words: a call at mf uses s calls at f on volume V/W, so cost per volume grows by s/W<m. This matches the paper's route to F_k <= (s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), and S3's method mentions row streams. Missing: the additive O(1) node term and fixed-tape schedule, the W^k row divisibility, and the D<-D-H, H<-H+D, D<-H-D completion of the interchange.

S2.1 states the lemma's content: two disjoint u-bit fields of a Cartesian-product array are interchanged in O(Vu^tau) with fixed tau<1. The reduction from arbitrary width to the power-width procedure (row field, padding, base-m pieces) is not shown.

The only allusion is generic: edges reduce to smaller calls of the same procedure. There is no conversion of residual kernels to coordinate kernels via P_M, no child count s_c of C^{tensor f}, and no recovery H_0 = b S C S. I was unsure whether this generic allusion should count and chose the lower credit short of absent.

No step concerns the whole-chunk shifts with correction of exceptional addresses that implement the binary changes of basis. The plan does not carry over the intro's sentence about them (lines 176-179).

S3.4's generic recursion covers the layer only implicitly; the plan does not even say the parameter counts selected axes. It has no node overhead O((eK)^tau+1), no leaf cutoff e<d^beta, no q_0 row chunks, and no unrolling to d^{lambda'}.

S2.2 gives H_0 on one selected bit per chunk at cost O(Vd^{lambda'}). It says 'each of d chunks' where the paper allows at most d (1<=D<=d). It omits exact Gaussian-dyadic evaluation with a single final truncation, the error bound below sqrt2*2^{-p}, and K=floor(d^c).

S4.5 and S4.6 give the construction: powers of y as roots of unity, and forward transforms whose frequency order is retained and consumed by the opposite transform, built from fast layers and interchanges. Missing: omega_t=y^{2r/t}, F^+F^-=t^{-1}I, the bit-reversed layout L, the exact counterparts LBF^- and F^+B^{-1}L^{-1}, the error and the cost.

S4.7 names signed packing and the established O(n log n) multiplier as a subroutine. It does not state the evaluation at B_0=2^{4p}, the centered-residue recovery, the reduction mod y^r+1, or the O(rp log(rp)) cost.

Together S4.5-S4.7 give the construction: two forward transforms in a common order, pointwise ring products, and an opposite transform consuming that order. The normalization (f*g)/(rM), the commuting identity P(LBu,LBv)=LB P(u,v), the error and the cost are absent.

S4.2 states the content correctly in words: each prime-length transform is expressed through a power-of-two tensor transform with the permutations kept inside the identity. It gives no P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA, no condition theta>p/alpha^4, no tensor form with gamma, and no costs.

S4.3 states the first half: Bluestein's chirp turns the middle transform, with its target permutation, into normalized cyclic convolution. There is no chirp formula. The second half, that the retained source permutation R cancels across the two forward transforms, product and opposite transform, is missing from the plan (paper lines 206-208).
Only kappa=2^{-182} (S0) and 'distinct prime cyclic axes' (S4.1) appear. There are no sizes b, p, d, K, T, r, no prime-existence argument, and no fixed rational choice of exponents.

S4.1 states correctly that a Chinese-remainder map places the coefficients on distinct prime cyclic axes and preserves convolution. It omits the map x->prod x_i^{mu_i}, its triangular mixed-radix form and the controlled-shift implementation with its cost.

S4.4 states correctly that the twist makes the last cyclic coordinate a polynomial mod y^r+1 whose negative wrap gives the cyclic wrap after untwisting. It does not give x_d->zeta y with zeta=e^{pi i/r}, the wrap check, or M_C(f,g)=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(...)=(f*g)/T.

S4's method lists the chain of reductions, ending in rounding and carries. The source-transform composition 2^gamma B_0 Q F_t A = R F_s, its conjugate F^+, and the algorithm's steps (two source transforms, pointwise product, opposite transform, scaling by S and 2^{2b+4}S) are not stated.

S4.8 states the conclusion correctly: after removing normalizations and scales the error is below 1/2, so rounding and carries give the exact product. It has no error chain (E_s, E_w, 448b 2^{-b+gamma}) and does not say why p=6b and gamma<=b/4 are needed.
S0 states the final bound O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}) with kappa=2^{-182}. There is no cost table, no normalization by Tp, no margins g_i, and no reason why the minimum margin is 2kappa.
S0 relies on the nlogn-conjecture page and its motivation mentions n log n. No step states the eventual lower bound or why the power saving refutes it.

errors.says: For the bit procedure the endpoint operator is the address shear (H,D)->(H+D,D), cheap by lower-triangular factorization.
errors.paper: The endpoint shear H<-H+D is produced by the network: the frames Phi_M telescope to Phi_{I_m}. Lower-triangular factorization (Lemmas lem:lower-lower and lem:matrix-shear) implements each edge's shear Phi_{A_e} with rank(A_e) recursive interchanges. Applied directly to the full-rank I_m it would need m calls and give no saving. The paper's intro says only that two further linear-cost updates complete the interchange.

errors.says: H_0 is applied on one bit position in each of d address chunks.
errors.paper: The same bit position is selected in each of at most d equal-width chunks (1<=D<=d).

chain: At headline level the tree follows the paper's route: the two procedures (S2), the frame/network/rank-deficit recursion (S3), then the chain CRT -> resampling -> chirp -> twist -> synthetic ring convolution -> exact recovery (S4). Every step is an intro-level paraphrase with no sub-derivation, so the main bound is asserted, not reached. The chain is thinnest at the finite network's subspace budget (L<N/2 giving s<Wm), the phase-frame recursion and packed bit additions for the numerical layer, the cancellation of the source permutation, and the cost table that turns these savings into kappa=2^{-182}.
